slides.0.title: Meet Provence and Corsica
slides.0.subtitle: From the Greek founding of Marseille to French rule: the history of two Mediterranean regions
slides.1.title: Provence: from the Greeks to the AOC
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Greeks and Romans
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Greeks founded Marseille around 600 BC, so wine has been made here for at least 2,600 years; the Romans arrived around 125 BC and made it their first province beyond the Alps, and the name Provence comes from "Provincia" (Wikipedia)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Phylloxera and the railway
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Phylloxera devastated the vineyards at the end of the 19th century and some growers replanted with high-yielding Carignan; railways then opened new markets such as Paris (Wikipedia)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: The 1955 Crus Classés
slides.1.highlights.2.content: On 20 July 1955 the Côtes de Provence named 23 Crus Classés estates, 22 years before the AOC; 18 still hold the status today (Wine With Seth, Wikipedia)
slides.1.content: Provence's wine history is older than France itself.
slides.2.title: Provence's appellation timeline
slides.2.highlights.0.title: 1936 and 1941
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Cassis was among the first six AOCs in 1936 (Wine With Seth); Bandol and Bellet received their AOCs on 11 November 1941 (Wine With Seth, INAO)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Côtes de Provence in 1977
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Côtes de Provence was a VDQS in 1951 and became an AOC by decree on 24 October 1977 (INAO, Wine With Seth)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Later AOCs
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Coteaux d'Aix-en-Provence became an AOC in 1985 (VDQS in 1956), Coteaux Varois in 1993 and Les Baux-de-Provence on 20 April 1995 (Wine With Seth, Wikipedia)
slides.2.content: Appellation status arrived late for the largest names.
slides.3.title: Corsica: Phocaeans, Genoa and France
slides.3.highlights.0.title: A Greek colony
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Greeks from Phocaea founded a colony at today's Aléria in the 6th century BC and brought vine cuttings; sources give different years (about 565 to 570 BC), so the date is not tested (Wine With Seth, Wikipedia)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Pisa and Genoa
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Pisa and then Genoa ruled the island; for about 500 years Genoa set harvest and winemaking laws and banned exports to ports other than Genoa (Wikipedia)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: After 1769
slides.3.highlights.2.content: France took Corsica in 1769; Napoleon was born that year in Ajaccio to a wine-producing family (Wikipedia)
slides.3.content: Five centuries of Genoese rule left their mark on Corsican grapes and place names.
Roughly when did the Greeks found Marseille?
Around 600 BC; the Romans arrived around 125 BC.
What does the name Provence come from?
The Romans called it Provincia Romana, shortened and evolved into Provence.
In which year did Côtes de Provence become an AOC?
24 October 1977; it was a VDQS in 1951.
How many Côtes de Provence Crus Classés were named in 1955?
In which year did France take Corsica?
Which was Corsica's first AOC, and when?
Patrimonio became Corsica's first AOC in 1968 (INAO: decree of 13 March 1968).
